newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Feb trade surplus expected to rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Feb trade surplus expected to rise.

text.p: Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus is expected to show a year-on-year rise in February for the first time in over two years on the back of the yen's recent weakening, economists said on Wednesday.
Economists' forecasts for the February trade surplus ranged from 630 billion yen to 831.3 billion yen. There was a surplus of 648.0 billion yen in February 1996.
If the data, to be announced on Monday, does show a rise in the surplus, it would be the first year-on-year increase since November 1994.
A rise in the surplus would mainly be due the weakening of the yen, which has accelerated Japan's exports while putting a brake on imports, economists said.
"It's the effect of the weak yen. The rise in exports, led by cars, is spreading to export industries as a whole," said Yoshito Sakakibara, vice president at Salomon Brothers Asia.

In the first 20 days of February, Japan's trade surplus rose 53.3 percent from the same period a year earlier. The data showed that exports had risen 15.2 percent while imports had risen 12.8 percent.
Economists said the trend of the rise in exports exceeding that of imports was more noticeable in quantitative terms.
DKB Research Institute expects Japanese exports in February to show a year-on-year increase of 3.2 percent in quantitative terms, against a 2.5 percent drop for imports.
But the research institute said that in yen-based terms, imports were expected to show a rise of 13.6 percent from a year earlier, topping the 5.4 percent rise expected in exports.
"The yen's weakening has led to a rise in the yen-based prices of imports and this is slowing down the rise in the trade surplus," an economist with DKB Research said.
A minority of economists who predicted a slight shrinkage in the surplus noted special factors.

An economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said a fire at Aisin Seiki, a car parts maker, on February 1 would likely have pushed down car exports in the latter half of the month. The firm supplies parts to Toyota Motor Corp.
"If it were not for the fire, the surplus would have shown a rise," said the economist.
Forecasts by individual research firms are as follows:
DKB RESEARCH 630.0 billion yen
DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL 632.8 billion yen
NCB RESEARCH INSTITUTE 654.0 billion yen
INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN 690.0 billion yen
MERRILL LYNCH JAPAN 692.0 billion yen
SALOMON BROTHERS 759.0 billion yen
DAIWA BANK RESEARCH 831.3 billion yen
